# 1 Samuel Chapter 27 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 166r-166v | **Source Image:** 1SA_027_page_001.jpg

---

**27:1** And-said David in-his-heart, "Now I-will-be-swept-away one day by-[the]-hand of-Sha'ul (Saul). There-is-nothing better for-me than that I-should-escape, yes-escape, to-[the]-land of-[the]-Pelishtim (Philistines), and-will-despair from-me Sha'ul (Saul) to-seek-me again in-all [the]-territory of-Yisra'el (Israel), and-I-will-escape from-his-hand."

**27:2** And-arose David, and-he-crossed-over, he and-six hundred man who [were] with-him, to Akhish (Achish) son of-Ma'okh (Maoch), king of-Gat (Gath).

**27:3** And-dwelt David with Akhish (Achish) in-Gat (Gath), he and-his-men, each and-his-household -- David and-his-two wives, Akhinoam (Ahinoam) the-Yizre'elit (Jezreelitess), and-Avigayil (Abigail) [the]-wife of-Naval (Nabal) the-Karmelitess (Carmelitess).

**27:4** And-it-was-told to-Sha'ul (Saul) that David had-fled to-Gat (Gath), and-he-did-not-continue again to-seek-him.

**27:5** And-said David to Akhish (Achish), "If, please, I-have-found favor in-your-eyes, let-them-give to-me a-place in-one of-[the]-cities of-the-field, and-I-will-dwell there. And-why should-dwell your-servant in-[the]-city of-the-kingdom with-you?"

**27:6** And-gave to-him Akhish (Achish) in-the-day the-that Tziqlag (Ziklag). Therefore Tziqlag (Ziklag) has-belonged to-[the]-kings of-Yehudah (Judah) until this day.

**27:7** And-was [the]-number of-the-days which dwelt David in-[the]-field of-[the]-Pelishtim (Philistines): days and-four months.

**27:8** And-went-up David and-his-men, and-they-raided to the-Geshurim (Geshurites) and-the-Gizrim (Girzites) and-the-Amaleqim (Amalekites), for they [were the]-inhabitants of-the-land, which [is] from-of-old, as-you-come to-Shur and-unto [the]-land of-Mitzrayim (Egypt).

**27:9** And-struck David the-land, and-he-did-not-keep-alive man or-woman, and-he-took sheep and-cattle and-donkeys and-camels and-garments. And-he-returned, and-he-came to Akhish (Achish).

**27:10** And-said Akhish (Achish), "Where did-you-raid today?" And-said David, "Against the-Negev (south) of-Yehudah (Judah), and-against the-Negev (south) of-the-Yerakhmeli (Jerahmeelite), and-against the-Negev (south) of-the-Qeni (Kenite)."

**27:11** And-man or-woman David did-not-keep-alive, to-bring [them] to-Gat (Gath), saying, "Lest they-tell against-us, saying, 'Thus did David.'" And-thus [was] his-practice all the-days which he-dwelt in-[the]-field of-[the]-Pelishtim (Philistines).

**27:12** And-trusted Akhish (Achish) in-David, saying, "He-has-made-himself-utterly-odious among-his-people, among-Yisra'el (Israel), and-he-will-be to-me a-servant forever."

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **27:1** -- הִמָּלֵט אִמָּלֵט (I-should-escape, yes-escape): Infinitive absolute + imperfect construction expressing David's resolved determination. The verb נִלְחַץ is not used here; rather אֶסָּפֶה (I-will-be-swept-away), Nif'al of ספה, echoing the very fate David assigned to Sha'ul in 26:10.
2. **27:2** -- אָכִישׁ בֶּן־מָעוֹךְ (Akhish son of-Ma'okh): David's second flight to Gath. His first attempt (21:11-16 [Eng. 21:10-15]) ended in his feigning madness. Now with 600 warriors, he comes as a military asset, not a lone fugitive.
3. **27:6** -- The editorial note "until this day" (עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה) indicates a source written while Ziklag was still held by the Judahite royal house, suggesting pre-exilic composition for this material.
4. **27:7** -- יָמִים וְאַרְבָּעָה חֳדָשִׁים (days and-four months): The Leningrad Codex reads "days" (יָמִים) without specifying a number, likely meaning "a year and four months" per the Hebrew idiom where יָמִים alone can signify a full year (cf. Lev 25:29).
5. **27:8** -- הַגְּשׁוּרִי וְהַגִּזְרִי (the-Geshurites and-the-Girzites): The Girzites (גִּזְרִי) are otherwise unknown. The Leningrad Codex Ketiv is גזרי; some manuscripts read גרזי. These were pre-Israelite inhabitants of the Negev corridor.
6. **27:10** -- David's deception is elaborate: he claims to have raided Judahite and allied territories (Negev of Judah, Jerahmeelites, Kenites), when in fact he raided Israel's enemies. This convinces Akhish that David has burned all bridges with his own people.
7. **27:12** -- הַבְאֵשׁ הִבְאִישׁ (he-has-made-himself-utterly-odious): Another infinitive absolute construction, Hif'il of באשׁ (to stink). Akhish's conclusion -- that David will serve him "forever" (עַד עוֹלָם) -- represents the height of his deception.

-- EMET
